newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LEWIS ON SONG FOR SUNDAY CHAMPIONS SURREY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LEWIS ON SONG FOR SUNDAY CHAMPIONS SURREY.

text.p: Discarded England all-rounder Chris Lewis struck a winning note for Sunday League champions Surrey on the day they made music at The Oval.
Lewis stroked an unbeaten 68 as Surrey snatched a three-wicket last-ball win over Somerset, but it was the musical dimension added to the game for which it is most likely to be remembered.
In a move that mirrored a New Zealand innovation during their recent one-day matches against England's touring team, Surrey introduced musical accompaniments for incoming batsmen.
They walked out to the sound of their chosen pop music, but Somerset seemed determined to be party poopers as the home county attempted to give fresh appeal to the 40 overs competition.
Despite scoring only 180, Somerset reduced Surrey from 43 for one to 69 for five before Lewis struck his 68 off 64 deliveries to leave the visitors facing the music.
Australian Tom Moody made a majestic 89 off 97 balls to guide Worcestershire to a composed seven-wicket success against last season's runners-up Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.

Captain Moody put Notts in to bat in seaming conditions and they struggled to 183 for eight, which Worcestershire surpassed with eight balls to spare after the Australian and Graeme Hick put on 102 in 18 overs for the second wicket.
Graham Lloyd raced to Lancashire's equal highest individual Sunday League score, hitting 134, as Durham were beaten by 57 runs at Old Trafford.
Lloyd smashed his runs from 85 deliveries to match the score by former West Indies captain Clive Lloyd for the county against Somerset in 1970.
England middle order batsman John Crawley weighed in with 83 in a home total of 268 for six, to which Durham replied with 211 for five.
Leicestershire slumped to a dismal 125 for nine at home to Gloucestershire and lost by 111 runs.
Only tailender Gordon Parsons offered resistance for Leicestershire with 41 not out, Gloucestershire's new Tasmanian signing for the season, Shaun Young, snapping up two for 10 from six overs.
